outcome_text: 85% of enrolled youth attended at least 30 program sessions during the school year.
Parents reported feeling more confident that their child has a safe, supervised place to go after school.
Youth who attended the program regularly improved their homework completion habits.
Students reading below grade level increased their oral reading fluency by an average of 12 words per minute.
Tutors completed 40 hours of training and began weekly one-on-one sessions with assigned students.
Youth feel more confident reading aloud in front of their class.
70% of participants reported increased interest in pursuing a career in a STEM field.
Youth designed and built a functioning robot and presented it at the regional competition.
Girls' enrollment in advanced STEM electives at partner schools increased 15% over the prior year.
Participants demonstrated improved technical skill on their instrument as measured by a jury assessment.
The program presented 12 community performances this season.
Youth reported feeling more comfortable expressing themselves creatively and made new friends in the program.
Participants increased their weekly physical activity to at least 60 minutes on 5 or more days.
Coaches learned to lead a new conflict-resolution curriculum during pre-season training.
Youth showed improved sportsmanship and teamwork during games.
85% of mentor-mentee matches remained active for at least 12 months.
Mentees reported a stronger sense of belonging and connection to a caring adult.
Youth-mentor pairs met weekly, and mentees' school attendance improved over the program year.
Seniors submitted the FAFSA and at least one college application by January 1.
90% of participants enrolled in a two- or four-year college the fall after graduation.
Students increased their understanding of the financial aid process, including grants and loans.
Youth obtained subsidized summer employment and completed at least 120 paid work hours.
Participants demonstrated improved workplace communication and professionalism.
75% of program graduates were employed or enrolled in postsecondary education six months after completion.
Participants opened a savings account within three months of completing the workshop.
Youth increased their knowledge of budgeting, credit, and saving as measured by a pre/post quiz.
Families reported feeling more confident managing household finances.
Youth organizers led a campaign that resulted in a new city ordinance extending youth curfew hours during summer months.
Participants increased their knowledge of the voter registration process and registered eligible peers.
Youth reported an increased sense that they can influence decisions in their community.
Students correctly identified 80% more native plant and animal species on post-program assessments compared to pre-tests.
Youth completed a 3-day backpacking expedition and demonstrated leadership in group decision-making.
Participants reported increased comfort and confidence spending time outdoors.
Students receiving counseling showed a reduction in self-reported anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7 screener.
Referrals to the school-based clinician increased 20% following staff training on warning signs of distress.
Youth developed healthier coping strategies for managing stress.
Participants reported delaying the age of first alcohol use.
Youth increased their knowledge of the health risks associated with vaping and e-cigarette use.
The program delivered prevention curricula to 500 students across 6 partner schools this year.
Students demonstrated improved conflict de-escalation skills in post-training role-play assessments.
School staff reported a decrease in physical altercations following implementation of the restorative justice program.
Youth feel safer walking to and from school.
70% of youth released from detention had no new adjudications within 12 months of release.
Participants secured stable housing and enrolled in school or employment within 30 days of release.
Youth improved their ability to set and work toward personal goals.
Youth aging out of care obtained a state-issued ID, Social Security card, and birth certificate before turning 18.
Young people reported having at least one permanent, supportive adult connection.
Participants increased their independent living skills, including cooking, budgeting, and using public transit.
Youth exited the shelter into safe and stable housing.
Participants engaged in case management and reduced the number of nights spent unsheltered.
Youth reported an increased sense of safety and trust in program staff.
Teen mothers continued or re-enrolled in school within 6 weeks of giving birth.
Parenting participants demonstrated improved knowledge of infant health and safety practices, including safe sleep.
Young parents feel more confident in their parenting abilities and less isolated from peers.
Youth reported a decrease in feelings of isolation after joining the support group.
Participants identified at least one trusted adult they could turn to for support.
The program fostered a more welcoming and affirming environment for LGBTQ+ youth.
Youth with disabilities participated in inclusive recreational activities alongside peers without disabilities.
Parents of children with disabilities reported increased knowledge of their child's rights under IDEA.
Participants demonstrated improved self-advocacy skills during IEP meetings.
Families increased their understanding of the U.S. school enrollment and healthcare systems.
Adult participants improved their English language proficiency by one CASAS level.
Youth reported feeling more connected to their new community.
Children demonstrated age-appropriate developmental milestones on the Ages & Stages Questionnaire.
Home visitors conducted monthly visits, and caregivers reported increased confidence supporting early literacy at home.
First-time mothers initiated and sustained breastfeeding for at least six months.
Families increased household income while parents completed occupational skills training.
Parents reported improved communication and reduced conflict with their children.
Caregivers connected to at least two new community resources or public benefits.
Households reported reduced food insecurity as measured by the USDA six-item screener.
The pantry distributed 50,000 pounds of food to 1,200 households this quarter.
Families increased their weekly consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables.
Participants exited transitional housing into permanent housing and maintained it for at least six months.
Households reduced their rent burden to below 30% of income.
Case managers helped clients complete and submit applications for housing choice vouchers.
Households received a laptop and broadband subsidy and reported increased ability to complete tasks online.
Participants improved their digital literacy skills, including email and video conferencing.
Older adults reported feeling less anxious using technology.
Youth grew in their faith and felt a stronger connection to their spiritual community.
Participants attended weekly youth group and volunteered at least once in the community this semester.
Teens reported increased trust in adult mentors within the congregation.
Campers demonstrated improved swimming proficiency, advancing at least one skill level.
Youth reported making new friends and feeling a sense of belonging at camp.
4-H members completed their project record books and presented them at the county fair.
Adolescents increased their knowledge of nutrition and made healthier food choices in the school cafeteria.
Participants reduced recreational screen time to less than 2 hours per day.
See attached logic model for a full list of outcome measures.
Outcomes: Systems and Policy Change
The coalition secured a new local ordinance restricting youth access to flavored tobacco products.
Member organizations reported increased collaboration and shared data across systems serving youth.
